messages:
Margo (CS): heads-up from today's Velosphere onboarding call — they really like the perf but surfaced 3 items that could affect renewal if we don't address them soon. dropping notes here.
Victor (CSM): TL;DR: pilot at ~40k tokens/day, finance wants per-campaign cost breakdowns; ops hit duplicate events from retries; product team wants clearer per-route latencies. risk = medium-high.
Margo (CS): direct asks from their eng lead:
```
- server-side webhook retry with idempotency header support
- request tagging for per-campaign cost attribution (exportable)
- per-route latency percentiles (p50/p95) in console or CSV
```
Margo (CS): they experienced a webhook 502 -> client retried -> duplicate downstream actions. they'd prefer Redwood to optionally handle retries + a dead-letter flow so their infra doesn't double-process. :grimacing:
Neil (PM): good signal. can we get a sample of the failing request/headers and the count of routes? helps scope.
Margo (CS): paste from their eng: 
```
curl -v -X POST https://hooks.velo.example/ingest -H "X-Idempotency: 123e4567" -H "X-Campaign: spring-promo" -d '{"route":"scoring","id":98765}'
```
Margo (CS): they run ~6 routes: scoring, enrichment, summarization, embeddings, rerank, billing-annotate. scoring is main pain.
Ashley (Eng): quick engineering read: idempotency-based retries + DLQ is doable but needs request-id propagation and a DLQ write path. per-route retry settings require routing-layer config and metrics tagging. minimal viable work around 2 sprints if we include DLQ retention policies.
Victor (CSM): from customer priority POV: CFO wants cost attribution ASAP; ops wants retry/idempotency to avoid duplicates. if we ship cost-tagging MVP first it reduces immediate pressure.
Neil (PM): suggested split: (A) cost-tagging MVP (header passthrough + export), (B) per-route observability improvements (p50/p95), (C) server-side retry + idempotency + DLQ. what's the fastest win?
Ashley (Eng): fastest = header passthrough and include campaign tag in usage export (add x-rw-campaign). telemetry change + CSV export = ~1 sprint. observability p50/p95 per-route = another sprint if we reuse existing metrics pipeline. retries infra = heavier.
Margo (CS): I'll tell the customer we can prioritize cost export this week if we scope it. CFO asked for a CSV export by end of week.
triage-bot: created ticket RW-6221: "campaign-cost-tagging MVP for exports" assigned to Product; URL: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RW-6221 :white_check_mark:
Emma (Support): I've linked the support trace for the duplicate event: https://support.redwood.com/t/9876. it includes the 502 spikes and their retry logs.
Neil (PM): Ashley - can you post a short tech-note in RW-6221 outlining idempotency header format, expected DLQ behavior, and rough effort estimate by Thu? that'll help prioritize B/C.
Ashley (Eng): will add draft tech-note and effort estimate to RW-6221 by Thu.
Victor (CSM): I'll set customer expectation: cost-tagging MVP first, then follow with diag for retries + ETA.
Margo (CS): I'll create the acceptance criteria for the cost export ticket: header name, sample payload, CSV column mapping, and sample rows from their pilot. linking customer logs.
Margo (CS): sample acceptance criteria snippet: 
- Pass-through header `X-RW-Campaign` accepted and recorded
- Campaign field present in usage export CSV as `campaign_name`
- Export generation within 24h window on request
- Docs + example curl included
Victor (CSM): perfect. ping me when ticket has the sample CSV so I can validate with their CFO.
Margo (CS): will do. closing for now; will post updates after sprint planning. thanks everyone.
